summary: Design plus opt-in CPU prototype; no speed change (after = null). Roofline from checkpoint bytes: one step reads 2.4 GB at N=1, of which 1.69 GB dense weights are shared; ceiling x2.2 at 4 streams and x3.1-3.6 at 16 (SGLang's measured 157.5/219.9 is 95%/83% of it). Staged plan S1-S5 about 18.5 working days; expected 130-145 tok/s at 4 and 185-205 at 16 after S5, 105-120 at 4 after S3 (closes the vLLM gap at 4). The prototype lifts the refusal on CPU behind INTARSIA_RECURRENT_BATCH=1 and shows batched greedy output token- and logit-identical to solo; it also found 4 plumbing defects beyond batch.rs:374 (gated attention gate dropped, prefix reuse fails requests on recurrent slots, solo prefill schedule differs, spec flag false).
lessons: The refusal at engine/batch.rs:374 is one of seven blockers; model/batch.rs rejects GDN, MoE and gated attention, and CUDA registers no rows_exact kernels.

The batch-consistency check (plan::check_batch_ops) fails the load when a batched step's fused-op multiset differs from the solo step: every fused decode op (fp8 pair, gated norm + fp8 out-proj) needs a multi-row form or a per-row run.

The 35B step is 1.69 GB shared dense weight vs 0.57 GB routed experts and 0.13 GB per-sequence GDN state: expert grouping is worth only +2% at 4 streams, +16% at 16; GDN state must be read in place (gather/scatter would add 3x state traffic).
vLLM's flat 105 from 2 to 16 streams is its --max-num-seqs 2 production setting, not a limit; the fair bar is SGLang.
